name: Jobab
title: King of Edom and descendant of Esau
summary: Jobab is a name that appears several times in the Bible. The most prominent Jobab was the son of Zerah from Bozrah, who reigned as king of Edom. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as one of the early kings who ruled over Edom before Israel had any king.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Joktan's lineage
keyEvents.description: One Jobab is mentioned as the son of Joktan in the genealogy after the flood, as one of the patriarchs of early peoples.

keyEvents.title: Jobab becomes king of Edom
keyEvents.description: After King Bela, son of Beor, died, Jobab, son of Zerah from Bozrah, became king of Edom. He was one of the eight kings who reigned in Edom before Israel received their kings.

keyEvents.title: Death of Jobab and his successor
keyEvents.description: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites became king after him, showing the shifts of power among Edom's early kings.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in the genealogical register of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Jobab's role as king of Edom is confirmed in the parallel genealogical register of Chronicles, which repeats the list of Edomite kings from Genesis.

keyEvents.title: The list of Edomite kings as historical context
keyEvents.description: Jobab is part of the important list of eight kings who ruled in Edom before any Israelite king, providing historical context for the relationship between the descendants of Esau and Jacob.
